decisions.title: Use direct modular operations for equipment administration
decisions.context: Equipment changes are local and governed by record-level validation and audit

options.description: Plain module with transaction operations and one datastore

scenarioResults.evidence: Record mutation and audit append share one transaction

benefits: Low ceremony and one obvious write authority
costs: The module must be split if unrelated change reasons emerge
risks: Richer behavior may be recognized late

options.description: Rich domain model with aggregate and repository abstractions

scenarioResults.evidence: An aggregate can also coordinate record and audit behavior

benefits: Explicit home for future interacting rules
costs: Unjustified abstractions and mapping for current CRUD
options.reversalEvidence: Several interacting invariants require richer behavior ownership

decisions.decision: Use one equipment operations module with direct transaction scripts
tradeoffsAccepted: Reopen structure if interacting rules or independent release needs emerge
consequences: Equipment writes remain behind one in-process module boundary
reviewTriggers: A rule coordinates multiple equipment records or independent owners
